clue.text: Finding there's little cash about, a good man gets most acrimonious

parts.note: a sou was a French coin of tiny value, hence little cash
re is Latin-derived for concerning, about
St, short for saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a saintly man becomes bitter when money is short.
explanation.definitionFit: Sourest is the superlative of sour, meaning most bitter or ill-tempered.

clue.text: Don't carry on! See the timekeeper

parts.note: an order to cease is stop
to watch is to see

explanation.surface: An order to halt and a pointer towards the official who keeps time at a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopwatch is a device for timing events precisely, a keeper of time.

clue.text: Opposing some reform, being over-suspicious of change

indicators.note: some of the following word's letters are taken, a run concealed inside it

explanation.surface: Someone resists a reform because they are wary of any change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' signals that the letters are taken from inside 'over-suspicious'; the rest of the clue paints the picture of a reactionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Versus means against, as in one side opposing another.

clue.text: Went round the bend when manoeuvred into a difficult position

definitions.meaning: trapped with no way out, as a hunted animal is

explanation.surface: A driver takes a bend and gets trapped in an awkward spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a corner on a road, and being trapped in a corner by an opponent, share one past tense.

clue.text: Popular stories of moneyed people?

parts.note: read as tales of the day that are widely told, then as the everyday bank holdings that people with money keep

explanation.surface: A question about gossip columns devoted to the rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular stories' suggests news or tales; the moneyed people point to banking, where these are everyday cheque-book holdings.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyday bank holdings used for payments go by this name, and the words also suggest tales in circulation now.

clue.text: A person at the bank interested in liquid assets

definitions.text: A person at the bank interested in liquid assets

parts.words: A person at the bank interested in liquid assets
parts.note: reads like a banker keen on cash, but the bank is a riverside and the liquid is water

explanation.surface: A bank official keen on cash that can be drawn quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Bank and liquid assets suggest finance; the clue really means someone living by a river, whose assets are its waters.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes someone or something living on a riverbank, concerned with the flowing water.

clue.text: The ordinance doctors cited

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Physicians quote a regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctors' looks like the subject of the sentence but is a verb telling you to rearrange CITED.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or ordinance issued by an authority.

clue.text: Jealous of a character with five financial liabilities

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of type width, a character's space
V is five in Roman numerals
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: Someone resents a person who owes little money.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a typesetting measure the width of a letter N.
explanation.definitionFit: Envious means resentful of what others have, a synonym of jealous.

clue.text: Tories may well get offensive

indicators.note: hints that the party's letters may well end up in another order

explanation.surface: A political jibe that Conservatives are likely to turn aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective about the Tories, but it is a noun: a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A sortie is a sudden attack by troops from a defended position, an offensive.

clue.text: Delay can be caused by a traveller habitually coming back without one

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative

indicators.note: here means outside, so the turned word wraps round the numeral
says this word is read from end to start

parts.note: ever can mean always, habitually
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A salesman who keeps returning without one item causes hold-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking: REVE (EVER read backwards) goes round I to make RIEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve is a postponement or delay of a punishment.

clue.text: He'll move the lowest ranking sailor into decent accommodation

indicators.note: the sailor goes into the decent word, as into lodgings

parts.note: proper means respectable, decent
OS is an ordinary seaman, the lowest naval rank

explanation.surface: A junior seaman is moved into respectable quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' is meant as at a meeting: the person who moves a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: At a meeting, the person who moves a motion puts it forward for debate.

clue.text: Allowance made for an offender inside admitting nothing

parts.note: a rat is a betrayer or wrongdoer

indicators.note: letting something in, so the word for inside takes in the nothing

parts.note: in means inside
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A prisoner who confesses to nothing still gets his share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' looks like prison slang, but it is just IN, which takes in O.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is a fixed allowance of food or supplies.

clue.text: A criminal who takes simpletons in

parts.note: an ass is a fool, a simpleton, and the plural gives two
the second of the two fools

explanation.surface: A swindler who cons gullible people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes in' suggests conning, but the killer takes lives; 'simpletons' gives two ASSes.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, someone guilty of a grave crime.

clue.text: Cross note written about party-going youngsters

indicators.note: the note is set down around the youngsters

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
ravers go to raves, wild parties

explanation.surface: An angry letter is penned complaining of young partygoers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, but it is a verb, to go across.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across something.

clue.text: Finish ahead of the French, scheming as ever

parts.note: end means finish
les is French for the plural the
sly means crafty, scheming

explanation.surface: A plotter finishes ahead of the French, cunning as always.
explanation.definitionFit: Endlessly means without stopping, for ever.

clue.text: Like a star taking a certain measure in the country

indicators.note: the country takes in the measure

parts.note: a state is a nation, a country
an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: A celebrity measures up across the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellate means star-shaped, radiating from a centre like a star.

clue.text: State shortly the jerk is to be pitied

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania, a US state
a tic is an involuntary twitch, a jerk

explanation.surface: Briefly put, the idiot deserves sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' looks like a fool, but it is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic means arousing pity, deserving sympathy.

clue.text: A good book about fruit providing sustenance

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
NT is the New Testament, part of the Bible

explanation.surface: A Bible and fruit nourish someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is food, nourishment, sustenance.

clue.text: The free-thinker hates it, oddly enough

indicators.note: the letters are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A rationalist detests something, surprisingly.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist rejects religious belief, a free-thinker in the old sense.

clue.text: Combine in one flat once properly organised

indicators.note: the letters are put in proper order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice about sorting out a single flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To conflate is to merge two things into a single whole.

clue.text: Figure this should reduce discomfort

definitions.meaning: something that numbs, a numbing agent

explanation.surface: A digit and a painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is NUMB plus ER, a thing that deadens feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure is a numeral; and an anaesthetic that deadens sensation could jokily be called a numb-er.

clue.text: To edge back outside first could be a bit of a bloomer

indicators.note: the turned edge goes outside the first
the word for edge is read from end to start

parts.note: a lip is a rim, an edge
1st, written IST, means first

explanation.surface: Turning the rim back first might be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LIP into PIL, which goes round IST. 'bloomer' looks like a mistake; it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The pistil is the female seed-bearing part of a flower, a bit of a bloom.

clue.text: Instruct in the correct presentation of trout

indicators.note: the fish's letters are re-presented in a new order

explanation.surface: Teach how to serve fish properly.
explanation.definitionFit: To tutor is to teach or instruct privately.

clue.text: Exposed a number entering with no invitation

indicators.note: the number goes into the uninvited word

parts.note: unasked means not invited
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A gatecrasher is revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmasked means revealed, with a disguise removed.

clue.text: Check all the others shower

parts.note: the rest means the remainder
rain falls in a shower

explanation.surface: Inspect everyone else's wet weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back, to check.

clue.text: Let in possibly about a quarter to sign up

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the quarter
the letters could possibly be rearranged

parts.note: S is south, a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Admitting about a quarter of applicants to join up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns LETIN into ENLIT, which goes about S.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to join the forces, to sign up.

clue.text: Really dark lead — inferior

parts.note: the star is the lead actor
less means lower, inferior

explanation.surface: A judgment on a gloomy leading performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A starless sky has no points of light, so is very dark.
